blocks.x: It may be a bit early for the pantomime season but the Holte End enjoyed acclaiming their heroes and villains as Aston Villa won at home for the first time this season with their biggest victory in European competition. Every touch for Mason Greenwood, playing his first game in England since January 2022, was booed, but even louder applause was reserved for Aston Villa’s rediscovered attacking prowess.

Johan Manzambi celebrated his 21st birthday by opening the scoring on his first Champions League appearance, before Nicolas Jackson took the game beyond Fenerbahce’s reach with two more goals before half-time to help banish any fears about playing in front of the demolished North Stand.

With Prince William cheering on from the stands, Ross Barkley made this a night to remember as he scored twice, the first goal from a penalty earned by Manzambi, and Tammy Abraham helped Villa score six in a game for the first time since beating Brighton in 2023. No team has won more games (15) in European competition since the start of last season.

Villa’s supposed hex about playing in front of the empty North Stand was put to bed as they scored three times at the end of the ground that is being redeveloped this winter. “Greenwood, Greenwood, what’s the score,” echoed around the three packed stands at Villa Park. Chants of a less salubrious nature were also given regular renditions. This was the former England forward’s first game in this country since he played in Manchester United’s 1-0 win against West Ham United in nearly five years ago.

blocks.c: Johan Manzambi scores his deflected goal for the opener

blocks.x: Greenwood was charged in 2022 with attempted rape, controlling and coercive behaviour and assault occasioning actual bodily harm. The Crown Prosecution Service discontinued the case in February 2023 after key witnesses withdrew their involvement and new material came to light. The player had denied the charges.

He had played for Marseille in a friendly against Villa 14 months ago, when he allegedly spat at Amadou Onana. So it was no surprise when his name was booed as the teams were announced and at every subsequent involvement.

Far more palatable was the freedom with which Villa played. Jackson now has five goals for Unai Emery’s team since signing from Chelsea for £65m in the summer while Manzambi, a £59.5m capture from Freiburg, was a joy to watch in the No 10 role, combining deft touch with wiry physicality. “My first Champions League game and my first goal, on my birthday,” he said. “My family are here. That’s very nice for me.”
The Switzerland international composed himself to score after Mattéo Guendouzi had inadvertently headed on John McGinn’s cross following a short corner.

blocks.c: Ross Barkley shares a high-five with Nicolas Jackson

blocks.x: Zion Suzuki twice saved well from Vedat Muriqi but Villa created umpteen chances themselves. Jackson, collecting Boubacar Kamara’s pass, struck home cleanly from the edge of the penalty area just after the half-hour mark before repeating the trick six minutes before the interval. In between, Oguz Aydin shot against the Villa bar, but, truth be told, Villa’s 11th successive home win in European competitions was already safely banked.

Villa’s free-scoring spell is in stark contrast to their start to the season, when they only managed one goal in their opening four games. Now they have scored at least three times in four of their past six matches.

Should they beat Viking here next Wednesday, Villa would be well on their way to qualifying from the league stage with nine points from three games. “We are being ambitious,” Unai Emery, the Villa manager, said. “We want to be protagonists in the Champions League.”

blocks.c: Nicolas Jackson scores Aston Villa’s third goal

blocks.x: Manzambi was tripped by Ismail Yuksek midway through the second half for the penalty from which Barkley made it 4-0, even if Jackson admitted he had fancied the chance to keep the match ball. “Yeah I wanted to take it but the most important thing is we win,” the striker told TNT Sports. “Hopefully next time I’ll get the hat-trick.”
The cheers that followed that goal were promptly matched by the jeers for Greenwood as he was substituted. The pantomime was over as a contest.

Barkley swiftly added a fifth with a deflected shot. But even before Abraham turned in Alysson’s cross for the sixth goal, some Villa minds were turning to Saturday evening’s trip to Newcastle United and the perennial autumnal challenge of resurrecting a difficult start to the league season. In Emery they trust.
